key_insight: The paper proposes a high-order ALE-SAV finite element scheme that preserves a discrete energy-dissipation law for sharp-interface two-phase Navier--Stokes flow on moving meshes.
engineering_relevance: This provides a stable, linear, and high-accuracy tool for simulating multiphase flows with evolving interfaces, such as bubbles, droplets, and free-surface dynamics.
method: Uses a scalar auxiliary variable (SAV) reformulation to handle surface and gravitational potential energies stably.
Introduces an energy-stable ALE transfer operator to control density-weighted kinetic energy across mesh motion.
Builds a fully discrete finite element method with modified energy-dissipation inequality and high-order accuracy in time and space.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports rising-bubble benchmark tests and shows second-order convergence in time with arbitrarily high-order convergence in space.
watch_item: The method is linear and stable, but practical performance may depend on careful implementation of the ALE transfer operator and moving-mesh handling.
paper_title: High-order energy diminishing ALE-SAV finite element methods for two-phase Navier--Stokes flow
